name: Legal-research label and scope evaluation
description: For annotated legal-research benchmark records, compare jurisdiction and citation identifiers and summarize independent applicability and scope reviews.

prediction.jurisdiction.description: Predicted jurisdiction label from the dataset's controlled vocabulary. Fictional examples use SYNTHETIC_JURISDICTION_A/B.

reference.jurisdiction.description: Independently curated jurisdiction label applicable to the benchmark question and source snapshot.

prediction.citation_ids.description: Citation identifiers supplied with the answer; IDs alone do not establish validity or authority.

reference.citation_ids.description: Curated required citation IDs for the item. Record date and source versions in metadata.

human_review.applicability_valid.description: Independent qualified-review annotation that the proposed authority applies to the benchmark's stated jurisdiction, date, and facts. The engine does not determine applicability or verify reviewer qualifications.

human_review.scope_score.description: Independent legal-research review, integer 0-4: 0 materially misstates or exceeds the annotated rule's scope; 1 omits central applicability conditions; 2 captures some conditions but has material scope gaps; 3 respects key conditions with minor omissions; 4 accurately preserves every annotated condition, exception, and uncertainty relevant to the task. This is a benchmark annotation, not legal advice.

metadata.dataset_version.description: Optional immutable dataset/split version for traceability. Not required or verified by this scorer.

metadata.model_version.description: Optional model/checkpoint version that produced the predictions. Not required or verified by this scorer.

human_review.reviewer_id.description: Optional independent reviewer identifier. The scorer does not authenticate the reviewer or validate qualifications; synthetic examples do not identify a real reviewer.

human_review.rubric_version.description: Optional version of the human-review instructions used to assign ratings. The scorer does not verify adherence to that rubric.

metrics.name: Jurisdiction-label accuracy
metrics.description: Fraction of predicted jurisdiction labels matching the curated reference.
metrics.limitations: Matching a label does not establish controlling law, current law, or legal applicability.

metrics.name: Required citation-ID recall
metrics.description: Mean fraction of curated required citation IDs present in the prediction.
metrics.limitations: Matches supplied IDs only. It does not open sources, verify that a source exists, or establish that a citation supports the answer. The metric does not verify that an authority is current, controlling, or correctly interpreted.

metrics.name: Imported applicability-review pass rate
metrics.description: Fraction of independent applicability-review annotations that are true.
metrics.limitations: This aggregates supplied review outcomes; it does not make an applicability determination. Preserve reviewer qualifications, task facts, and source dates outside the scorer.

metrics.name: Human-reviewed legal scope
metrics.description: Mean independently reviewed scope score normalized from 0-4 to 0-1.
metrics.limitations: This imports an independent review score; the engine neither performs the review nor verifies reviewer identity. Missing reviews are excluded and reduce coverage.

limitations: This is a reusable evaluation template, not an official benchmark scorer. All targets are unset; calibrate thresholds and minimum coverage on a representative held-out dataset. Scores are not automatically used as screening gates or RL rewards.
This template measures supplied benchmark labels and annotations. It does not validate legal advice, establish governing law, or replace qualified review.
Reference labels and citation sets require jurisdiction-, date-, and fact-specific curation. No source-law lookup is performed.
The fixtures use fictional jurisdictions, authorities, and review annotations. These are not official LegalBench tasks or scores.
Unused metadata and review-provenance fields are optional traceability suggestions; their presence, authenticity, and types are not validated unless a metric references them.
